parts.title: Word List
parts.content:
Word List

Detailed Meanings

😎
accelerate[aekselareit]v
To accelerate means to increase in speed.
→ When he stepped on the gas pedal, the motorcycle accelerated. » Though he had failed his driving test, he decided to try it anew.
😎
defect[difekt]n.
A defect is a part of something that is wrong or missing.
→ A ll these bottles have a defect and must be sent back to the warehouse.
😎
dreary[driari]adj.
If something is dreary, then it is dull, dark, and lifeless.
→ After the fire, this section o f forest is rather dreary.
😎
duplicate[dju:plakeit]v
To duplicate something means to copy it.
→ She duplicated her frie n d ’s movements like she was in front o f a mirror.
😎
electromagnetic[ilektroumaegnetik]adj.
If something is electromagnetic, it is related to electricity and magnetic fields.
→ Different colors o f lig h t come from different levels o f electromagnetic energy.
😎
electron[ilektron]n.
An electron is a particle in all atoms that has a negative electric charge.
→ » The number o f electrons in an atom determines the substance the atoms make.
😎
glide[glaid]v.
To glide means to fly on extended wings with little or no effort.
→ When the wind is blowing, birds can glide easily through the sky.
😎
ingenious[ind3i:njas]adj.
If someone is ingenious, then they are very smart.
→ Charles was the only person ingenious enough to repair the plane’s engines.
😎
innovation[inouveijan]n.
An innovation is a product or an idea that is new or very original.
→ Mrs. Johnson made a great innovation to the company’s business plan.
😎
innovative[Inouveitiv]adj.
If something or someone is innovative, they can think in creative ways.
→ Since Peter was so innovative, he was chosen to lead the science team. » The boat launched from the dock and floated down the river.
😎
meteorological[mi:tiaralad3ikal]adj.
If something is meteorological, it is concerned with the science of weather.
→ » The thunderstorm was so large that it became a great meteorological event. »In order to understand the weather, you have to study meteorology.
😎
penetrate[penatreit]v.
To penetrate something means to enter into it.
→ The knife easily penetrated the surface o f the orange.
😎
propulsion[prapAIJan]n.
Propulsion is the force that moves something forward.
→ The propulsion lifted the rocket into the sky.
😎
Simulate[slmjaleit]v.
To simulate something means to copy its actions or characteristics.
→ The French language teacher could simulate the accent o f a French citizen.
😎
Spur[spa:r]v.
To spur someone means to urge them into action.
→ The coach’s speech spurred her team into playing the best game o f their lives. Doctors sometimes use electric shock to stim ulate a patient’s heartbeat.
😎
tenacious[taneijas]adj.
→

questions.content: accelerate
questions.explanation: accelerate (v): to increase in speed. Similar to speed up.

questions.content:
You can hear because sound causes activity in the tiny hairs on the inside of your ear. [ 6 ]

Some worms are small enough to enter into the skin without being detected. [ 7 ]

She tried to copy the way her best friend dressed. [ 8 ]

The teacher offered the kids candy in order to urge them into finishing their homework. [ 9 ]

In science class, we learned about the particles in atoms that have a negative electric charge. [ 10 ]

questions.explanation: stimulates means to cause or to increase activity in.
penetrate means to enter into it.
duplicate means to copy it.
spur means to urge them into action.
electron is a particle in all atoms that has a negative electric charge.
anew means again and in a different way.
meteorology is the science that studies the weather.

sections.title: Exercise 3: Write C if the italicized word is used correctly. Write I if the word is used incorrectly.

questions.content: Just when you thought you’d caught up to Brian, he’d accelerate and quickly get away.
questions.explanation: accelerate means to increase in speed.

questions.content: The orchestra made a very tenacious sound, and many in the audience decided to leave.
questions.explanation: tenacious means not giving up easily, not a sound.

questions.content: Dan had duplicated the sculpture exactly. It now looked nothing like the original one.
questions.explanation: duplicated means copied exactly, so it would look like the original.

questions.content: Lions are dangerous hunters. They can glide through the air to capture their prey.
questions.explanation: lions do not glide (fly on wings).

questions.content: They had a picnic in the park and launched on small sandwiches and grapes.
questions.explanation: launched means to put into motion, not eaten.

questions.content: We made a small toy train that stimulated how real trains worked 100 years ago.
questions.explanation: should be simulated, not stimulated.

questions.content: Cellular phones are one of the most popular innovations in the world today.
questions.explanation: innovation is a new product or idea.

questions.content: The knight’s sword could not penetrate his opponent’s armor.
questions.explanation: penetrate means to enter into.

questions.content: The thought of his warm bed spurred the traveler on through the cold night.
questions.explanation: spurred means urged into action.

questions.content: We didn’t mind that our paintings got ruined. It was fun to start them anew.
questions.explanation: anew means again.

questions.content: Satellites are very important for gathering meteorological data.
questions.explanation: meteorological relates to weather science.

questions.content: Fish use their fins for propulsion in the water.
questions.explanation: propulsion is the force that moves something forward.

questions.content: I wish Dad wasn’t so innovative. He always comes into my room without knocking.
questions.explanation: innovative means thinking in creative ways, not entering without knocking.

questions.content: Some metals are attracted to other metals due to an electromagnetic force.
questions.explanation: electromagnetic relates to electricity and magnetic fields.

questions.content: Certain kinds of light can simulate flowers into producing seeds earlier than usual.
questions.explanation: should be stimulate, not simulate.

questions.content: John is so ingenious. He hasn’t passed a single test so far this year.
questions.explanation: ingenious means smart, which contradicts not passing tests.

questions.content: I’ve always been interested in meteors. That’s why I want to study meteorology.
questions.explanation: meteorology is weather, not meteors.

questions.content: The lake was frightening. The water was still and dreary.
questions.explanation: dreary means dull, dark, lifeless.

questions.content: Everyone who voted in the electron was given the day off of work.
questions.explanation: should be election, not electron.

questions.content: The new pot looked perfect. It was covered in new, shiny defects.
questions.explanation: defects are flaws, so it wouldn't look perfect.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
The Tenacious Inventor

A young student of meteorology was having a difficult time with an experiment. He was attempting to duplicate lightning in clouds. He had made a device that could simulate lightning. It worked by releasing an electromagnetic pulse into the cloud. This pulse, in turn, stimulated the electrons in the cloud’s particles. Then the electrons produced lightning.

But his meteorological experiment had a major defect. He couldn’t get the device into the sky.

He had tied it to balloons, but they had burst. He had shot the device from a cannon, but the force of the cannon had damaged it.

“You should give up,” his friends told him. “You’ll never get that thing into the air.”

But his friends’ criticisms only spurred him to try again. The student was very innovative, and at last, he thought that he had an innovation that would work. He attached wings to the device, and on one dreary day, when clouds blocked the light of the sun, he started his experiment anew.

He placed the device on a rocket and launched it into the sky. The propulsion of the rocket carried the device high into the air. The rocket accelerated into the clouds and then released the device. It glided on its wings through the clouds, and when it penetrated the center of a large black cloud, it emitted the electromagnetic pulse. And just as he had predicted, lightning shot from the cloud!

He called his professors, and the next day they came to watch. He successfully duplicated the experiment. His teachers were extremely impressed and called the student and his invention ingenious.

The student was given many awards and became a famous inventor. He had not given up. He had remained tenacious and succeeded.

sections.title: Part A: Mark each statement T for true or F for false.

questions.content: The student of meteorology had bought a device that simulated lightning in clouds.
questions.explanation:
Dịch: Cậu sinh viên ngành khí tượng học đã mua một thiết bị mô phỏng sấm sét trong các đám mây.
Giải thích: F. Đoạn 1 viết rằng: "He had made a device that could simulate lightning." (Cậu ấy đã tự tạo ra một thiết bị có thể mô phỏng sấm sét). Cậu ấy tự làm ra nó (made) chứ không phải đi mua (bought).

questions.content: The electromagnetic pulse stimulated the electrons in the cloud’s particles.
questions.explanation:
Dịch: Xung điện từ đã kích thích các electron trong các hạt của đám mây.
Giải thích: T. Đoạn 1 có miêu tả: "This pulse, in turn, stimulated the electrons in the cloud’s particles." (Xung này sau đó kích thích các electron trong các hạt của đám mây). Câu này hoàn toàn đúng.

questions.content: The student’s friends’ criticisms spurred him to try his experiment anew.
questions.explanation:
Dịch: Những lời chỉ trích của bạn bè cậu sinh viên đã thúc đẩy cậu ấy thử lại thí nghiệm của mình.
Giải thích: T. Đoạn 5 nói: "But his friends’ criticisms only spurred him to try again... he started his experiment anew." (Nhưng những lời chỉ trích của bạn bè chỉ thúc giục anh ấy thử lại lần nữa... anh ấy bắt đầu lại thí nghiệm của mình).

questions.content: It was a dreary day when the device glided into the clouds.
questions.explanation:
Dịch: Đó là một ngày ảm đạm khi thiết bị bay lượn vào trong những đám mây.
Giải thích: T. Trong đoạn 5 tác giả có nói: "and on one dreary day, when clouds blocked the light of the sun, he started his experiment anew." (và vào một ngày ảm đạm, khi những đám mây che khuất ánh sáng mặt trời, anh ấy bắt đầu lại thí nghiệm của mình).

questions.content: The propulsion of the rocket accelerated the speed of the lightning.
questions.explanation:
Dịch: Lực đẩy của tên lửa đã làm tăng tốc độ của tia sét.
Giải thích: F. Đoạn 6 cho biết lực đẩy của tên lửa dùng để đưa thiết bị lên cao: "The propulsion of the rocket carried the device high into the air." (Lực đẩy của tên lửa đã đưa thiết bị lên cao trong không trung). Tên lửa không hề làm tăng tốc độ của tia sét!

questions.content: What was the defect of the student’s meteorological experiment?
options: It couldn't get into the sky.
questions.explanation:
Dịch câu hỏi: Khuyết điểm trong thí nghiệm khí tượng của cậu sinh viên là gì?
Giải thích: Chọn A.
Đoạn 2 nêu rất rõ: "But his meteorological experiment had a major defect. He couldn’t get the device into the sky." (Nhưng thí nghiệm khí tượng của anh ấy có một khiếm khuyết lớn. Anh ấy không thể đưa thiết bị lên bầu trời).

questions.content: What innovation did the innovative student use to launch his device into the clouds?
options: He placed the device on a rocket and launched it into the sky.
He shot it from a cannon.
He carried it on a plane.
questions.explanation:
Dịch câu hỏi: Sáng kiến nào mà cậu sinh viên sáng tạo đã dùng để phóng thiết bị của mình vào các đám mây?
Giải thích: Chọn A.
Đoạn 6 viết: "He placed the device on a rocket and launched it into the sky." (Anh ấy đặt thiết bị lên một quả tên lửa và phóng nó lên bầu trời). Đây chính là cách anh ấy dùng để đưa thiết bị lên cao.

questions.content: For whom did the student duplicate his ingenious experiment?
questions.explanation:
Dịch câu hỏi: Cậu sinh viên đã làm lại thí nghiệm thiên tài của mình cho ai xem?
Giải thích: Chọn A.
Đoạn 7 có chi tiết: "He called his professors, and the next day they came to watch. He successfully duplicated the experiment." (Anh ấy đã gọi cho các giáo sư của mình, và ngày hôm sau họ đến xem. Anh ấy đã thực hiện lại thành công thí nghiệm). Vậy cậu ấy đã làm lại thí nghiệm cho các giáo sư (professors) xem.

questions.content: What did the device do when it finally penetrated the center of a large black cloud?
questions.explanation:
Dịch câu hỏi: Thiết bị đã làm gì khi cuối cùng nó cũng xuyên qua trung tâm của một đám mây đen lớn?
Giải thích: Chọn A.
Cũng ở đoạn 6: "...and when it penetrated the center of a large black cloud, it emitted the electromagnetic pulse." (...và khi nó xuyên vào trung tâm của một đám mây đen lớn, nó phát ra xung điện từ). Vậy thiết bị đã phát ra xung điện từ (emitted the electromagnetic pulse).

questions.content: What happened to the student because he was tenacious?
options: He succeeded and became a famous inventor.
He gave up and studied something else.
questions.explanation:
Dịch câu hỏi: Điều gì đã xảy ra với cậu sinh viên nhờ việc cậu ấy kiên trì?
Giải thích: Chọn A.
Đoạn cuối viết: "The student was given many awards and became a famous inventor. He had not given up. He had remained tenacious and succeeded." (Cậu sinh viên đã được trao nhiều giải thưởng và trở thành một nhà phát minh nổi tiếng. Cậu ấy đã không bỏ cuộc. Cậu ấy vẫn kiên trì và đã thành công). Nên nhờ kiên trì, cậu ấy đã thành công và trở nên nổi tiếng.
